_roadWidth: 50.0, TAKEN FROM tools/level4_geometry.json, which arrived with the plate. check_level4.py re-derives it off the painting -- casting normals through the track from each lane's centreline and taking the narrowest lane's median, the same method check_level3.py uses and for the same reason: the road has to fit its tightest stretch. It is NARROWER than level 3's 54.6 and level 1's 61, which matters for the hero and the line more than it does for the towers.
note: THE CONUNDRUM, and the second branching level. Grass on the west side, snow and rock on the east, and the map knows it: the seam runs roughly north-south through the merge. Every coordinate here comes from tools/level4_geometry.json -- two branch centrelines, a shared tail, the merge point, the road width and fourteen pads. Nothing was traced or typed by hand. Re-check it with `python3 tools/check_level4.py`. THREE THINGS WERE COMPUTED RATHER THAN COPIED, each stated in its own note below: the off-plate gateway at each end, the snap of each branch's last waypoint onto the merge point, and nothing else. THE MAP'S DEFINING PROPERTY IS THAT IT IS FRONT-LOADED: only three of the fourteen pads reach the shared tail at all, and between them they cover 45.3% of it. That is the terrain rather than an oversight -- east of the merge is snow, rock and ice pond, and none of it takes a tower. A player who lets a wave through the fork has almost no second chance at it, so level 4 is won or lost west of 737.
_spotRadius: 34, level 1's, 2's and 3's, and for the same reason level 3 records: world 1280 renders to 844 CSS px, so 34 world px is a 44.8 px tap diameter and anything under 44 pt is smaller than a thumb. Two pads need 2 x spotRadius between centres before their tap targets overlap, so 34 needs 68 -- and the closest pair here is 74.11 px, pads 8 and 9 on the snow shelf above the tail. It clears by 6.11, which is the tightest of the four levels and the reason check_level4.py fails under 74 rather than under 68.
_waypoints: THE SHARED TAIL east of the merge, which is the trunk every enemy finishes on. It is `shared` from the geometry file with one edit that is not a coordinate change: a gateway point is appended at x=1340 so enemies walk off the plate rather than vanishing at its edge. That point is NOT traced -- it is a new point on the line the tail is already travelling as it reaches x=1275, which is how levels 2 and 3 do it, and for the reason level 2 records: dragging the final traced point out instead would swing the closing segment off the paint. The tail's own first point already IS the merge point to 0.00 px, so no snap was needed at that end.
_lanes: TWO GATES, ONE EXIT, the same shape as level 3. Both branches run in from off the left edge and merge into the trunk at its waypoint 0. TWO EDITS, both documented rather than silent. FIRST, a gateway point is prepended to each branch, placed on the LINE OF THAT BRANCH'S FIRST TRACED SEGMENT rather than level with the opening, so an enemy walks in along the road it is already on. SECOND, a branch has to END at the join, which is what the lane engine expects, and each branch's last traced point was 1.07 px (upper) and 5.60 px (lower) short of the declared merge, so both were snapped onto it. Left alone an enemy would have stepped those pixels sideways as it transferred. THE GATEWAY DISTANCE IS THE ONE THING CHOSEN RATHER THAN COMPUTED, and it is chosen to make the two gates fair. The lower gateway sits at x=-60, level 3's figure. Placing the upper one there too would have left the upper route 3.55 px shorter -- 1475.42 against 1478.97 -- so it is pulled 3.55 px further out along its own line instead, to (-63.39, 68.33). Both routes now walk 1479.0 px gate to exit. THAT IS WORTH THE THREE PIXELS. Level 3's two routes came out equal to 0.03 px by accident of the trace, and its wave table leans on it: groups released from both gates on the same delay ARRIVE TOGETHER, so a split wave is a genuine two-front problem rather than a queue. Level 4's table leans on it the same way, and here it is arranged rather than lucky. The branches alone are 873.94 each and the trunk they share is 605.03. THE TRUNK IS 41% OF THE ROUTE AND ONLY 45.3% COVERED, which is what makes this level front-loaded.
_buildSpots: FOURTEEN PADS, copied from the geometry file untouched, and verified by check_level4.py on the three properties level 3 established. IN RANGE: each pad is 90 to 114 world px from the nearest lane centreline -- measured 90.9 to 111.0 -- against a tower range of 112, so every pad reaches the road it is meant to cover. APART: the closest pair is 74.11 px, over the 68 that spotRadius needs. ON GROUND: each pad's 24 px core sits on buildable ground -- not the track, an ice pond, rock, tree, the snowman, the bench, the sled or the fence. WHAT THE PADS DO NOT DO is cover the tail evenly, and that is deliberate: pads 0, 8 and 9 are the only three within 112 of the shared trunk (92.8, 102.1 and 101.8 px), and between them they reach 45.3% of it. Do not add pads to compensate -- east of the merge there is nowhere to put one, and the front-loading is the level's whole idea.
